learning.title: A PR with MISSING (not red) checks is probably CONFLICTING — check mergeStateStatus before touching CI
learning.body:
A CONFLICTING pull request gets no merge commit, so GitHub creates NO pull_request workflows at that head. The only runs that appear are pull_request_target ones (they execute from the base branch and need no merge commit). Symptom: the required aggregate is absent, description checks show green, and "gh pr checks" lists a fraction of the normal lanes — looking like a CI fault or missing wiring.
Found by dev-workflows' composition-root instrument on #514 (2026-11-17): gh run list --commit 49ea37c90 returned only two Description-policy pull_request_target runs; mergeable=CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus=DIRTY explained it. The conflict was one GENERATED file (packages/contracts/generated/contracts.json) gone stale after sibling merges (#513's contract rebind, #516).
Rule: for any PR whose checks are missing rather than red, read mergeStateStatus FIRST. Fix generated-file conflicts by merging main and regenerating (pnpm contracts:generate, or catalog:literals for catalog files), never by hand-merging the generated blob. Verify idempotency by running the generator twice — the second run must be a no-op.
